newsitem.title: GERMANY: KRUPP SEEN MAKING BID FOR THYSSEN.
newsitem.headline: KRUPP SEEN MAKING BID FOR THYSSEN.

text.p: German steel and engineering group Fried. Krupp AG Hoesch-Krupp said on Monday it was preparing to make a public statement after a German newspaper reported it was about to bid for rival Thyssen AG.

The daily Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung, in an advance report to appear on Tuesday, said Krupp was planning to make an offer to Thyssen shareholders. The offer was being prepared by Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, the investment arm of Deutsche Bank.
"We will not comment on these rumours now," Krupp spokesman Juergen Claassen told Reuters. "We will issue a press release shortly."
Thyssen said it was also preparing to make a statement.
It was not immediately clear when the statements would be released.
Both companies shares were suspended ahead of their statements.
The newspaper report recalled that the move was reminiscent of Krupp's spectacular takeover of rival Hoesch AG in 1991.

"We are unconcerned about this attempt," a Thyssen spokesman told Reuters. "This can only be an attempt on the part of Krupp to resolve its own considerable problems by tapping into Thyssen's reserves."
The spokesman added that Thyssen would use all "appropriate means" to counter any hostile takeover attempt and called a news conference for Tuesday afternoon.

A takeover of Thyssen by Krupp would be an "incomprehensible act in the style of the Wild West," the spokesman added, that would set off a restructuring programme that would cost tens of thousands of jobs.
A spokesman for Deutsche Morgan Grenfell in London said the bank never commented on market rumours as a general policy.
"And we would never comment on such a market rumour," said DMG spokesman Markus Will.
